name: Karvess (Ruin)
summary: The greatest ruin on Aurelith: an entire Concord city of woven glass turned to glass again in a single hour when the Rent passed beneath it. Towers, fountains, and ten thousand people preserved mid-motion, translucent and humming. The Censer forbids all expeditions. The Reeve wants one mounted.
original_role: capital of the Glass Kingdom (see factions/extinct-orders.json)

current_state.access: illegal by Censer writ; approachable only across forty miles of ash-farm and scrub
current_state.condition: structurally perfect, structurally dead — the glass sings on quiet nights and cracks spread each Mistshroud
current_state.inhabitants: Glass-Keepers tend the outer mouth; nothing else is confirmed

sites.name: The Singing Towers
sites.description: Nine glass towers still standing, leaning into the wind. On quiet nights they hum the same note heard in Hallord's sealed shaft and beyond the Veiled Sea's horizon.

sites.name: The Vitrified Square
sites.description: The central plaza: a market caught mid-morning, vendors and buyers fused into a single clear mass. Faces remain visible. Visitors report the faces are never quite where they remembered.

sites.name: The Glass-Keepers' Hut
sites.description: A rough stone shelter at the ruin's mouth where the Keepers rest, mark crack-maps, and leave water for travelers who will not admit they came.

sites.name: The Deep Gallery
sites.description: A collapsed entrance to underground galleries beneath the city. The glass around it is black, not clear. No expedition has returned from below; one came back, but that is disputed.

hazards: Vitrified ground fails without warning; three Censer surveyors have been swallowed since the Edict
The singing induces shared dreams in those who camp within earshot — always the same dream
Censer patrol airships (drift-barges) cross monthly; landing parties shoot first
adventure_hooks: Reeve Aldara's secret commission: map the Deep Gallery before the Censer learns the expedition exists
A Glass-Keeper offers crack-maps in exchange for retrieving a bell from the Vitrified Square — rung once, it might answer the towers
The humming stopped last week. Every faction noticed. None will say what they fear it means.
